## Latest signal

```{python}
longs = sig[sig["pos"] == 1].sort_values("rank")
shorts = sig[sig["pos"] == -1].sort_values("rank", ascending=False)
chips = lambda df, cls: "".join(f'<span class="chip {cls}">{r.market} · {r.ticker}</span>' for r in df.itertuples())
display(HTML(f"""
<div class="signal-card long" style="border-left-color:#2563eb">
  <div class="sc-left"><span class="sc-label">Portfolio</span>
    <span class="sc-state" style="color:#3b82f6">{len(longs)} LONG · {len(shorts)} SHORT</span></div>
  <div class="sc-right"><span>Signal date</span><b>{m['asof']}</b>
    <span class="sc-detail">{len(sig)} country ETFs ranked</span></div>
</div>
<b>Long</b><div class="chips">{chips(longs, 'long')}</div>
<b>Short</b><div class="chips">{chips(shorts, 'short')}</div>
"""))
```

### Composite score ranking

```{python}
dca_score_chart(sig)
```

<p class="legend-note">Green = long, red = short, grey = no position. Hatched bars marked ⊘ are on the no-hold list: they are ranked but never held, and the next eligible market takes their place. Hover over a bar for its rank.</p>

### Factor scores

```{python}
dca_factor_table(sig)
```

<p class="legend-note">Scores are cross-sectional z-scores. Green cells are above average and red cells below; darker means further from average.</p>

## Backtest

```{python}
s = bt["strategy"]
horizon_stat_tiles(s, 52, metrics=("CAGR", "Volatility", "Sharpe", "Max drawdown", "Calmar"))
```

<p class="asof">Weekly, `{python} f"{bt.index[1]:%b %Y}"` to `{python} f"{bt.index[-1]:%b %Y}"`. Net of trading and short-borrow costs. Equal-weight, dollar-neutral long / short, six markets per side, with the no-hold list applied throughout.</p>

## How it works

::: {.method}
- **Universe:** 30 country and regional equity ETFs across developed and emerging markets.
- **Factors:** each market is scored on **value**, **quality**, **growth** and **momentum**.
- **Model version:** version 3, live from November 2026. The value, quality and momentum scores now also draw on analyst forecasts and share-issuance data. The backtest applies the current model to the whole history.
- **Portfolio:** the strategy goes long the top-ranked markets and short the bottom-ranked, with equal weights on each side.
- **No-hold list:** a few markets can be ranked but excluded from holdings (currently `{python} " and ".join(sig.loc[sig["no_hold"].astype(bool), "market"]) or "none"`). The next eligible market fills the slot, so each side always holds six.
- **Rebalance:** weekly.
:::

:::
